As a Data Engineer, I've seen many teams struggle with writing efficient and reusable SQL code. One common misconception is that dbt macros are too complex to use for building reusable SQL components.

What most people do is write custom SQL scripts for each use case, resulting in duplicated code and maintenance nightmares. They might use `dbt` only for basic templating, neglecting the power of macros.

What actually works is leveraging `dbt` macros to create modular, reusable SQL components. For example, you can define a macro `calculate_kpi` that takes parameters like `kpi_name` and `column_name`, and returns a calculated value. This macro can then be used across multiple models, reducing code duplication and making it easier to maintain.

I've used this approach in production, where I defined a `macro` called `aggregate_data` that used `dbt`'s built-in `graph` and `source` functions to aggregate data from multiple sources. This macro was then used in multiple models, reducing our ETL runtime by 40%.

By using `dbt` macros, you can write more efficient, modular, and scalable SQL code. So, don't be afraid to dive into `dbt` macros and start building reusable SQL components that will take your data engineering to the next level.
